domain_label: Site Qualification, Proposal Integrity & Financing Literacy
purpose: How a residential solar seller turns a specific household's own utility data, rate structure, export-compensation regime, roof geometry, shade and service equipment into a right-sized system, a modeled (never promised) production and bill-comparison estimate whose every number is traceable to a captured artifact, and a disclosure-first walk-through of the cash, loan, lease and power-purchase financing classes plus the permitting and interconnection sequence, so the homeowner signs understanding what they bought.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator sells residential solar as a rep, dealer or referral partner and is paid a commission per installed system; the seller does not install, engineer or finance the system

utility tariffs, export-compensation regimes, incentive programs and consumer-protection rules differ by jurisdiction and utility and are revised frequently; every rule here is named as a class to verify against the current authoritative source in your jurisdiction
all knowledge here is educational and operational; eligibility for any tax credit, rebate or loan product is a question for the homeowner's own tax, legal or financial adviser

commissions, system prices, dealer fees, escalators and savings are described as mechanisms whose value is verified per deal from the installer, lender or utility document, never as figures asserted in advance
exclusions: sales-rep versus dealer versus referral model choice, commission and clawback structure, lead-generation channel economics and pipeline math — that is the market-models-and-lead-economics KB this one is built on top of

installer partner selection on build quality or install backlog, post-signature handoff and install-timeline management, cancellation recovery and the referral engine from happy installs — that is the installer-partnership-and-reputation KB this one hands off to

any engineering determination reserved to the installer and their licensed electrician or engineer: structural adequacy, final attachment and racking design, string design, code interpretation and the permit and interconnection filings themselves
contractor licensing, workers compensation, bonding and workmanship warranty obligations, which belong to the installing contractor and not to the seller
personalized financial, tax, legal or insurance advice, including whether a given homeowner can use a tax credit, which loan product they should take, or how a lease affects their estate
credit underwriting, application handling and adverse-action processes, which sit with the finance provider
commercial, utility-scale, ground-mount and off-grid design, and battery storage sizing beyond noting where storage changes export and tariff arithmetic

competency_questions.question: What has to be true before any number is allowed to appear in a proposal a homeowner keeps?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_PROPOSAL_CHARTER states the permitted sources for any shown quantity and the banned claim forms, and EVIDENCE_LEDGER shows how each number is tied to a dated artifact

competency_questions.question: How do I turn a household's bills into a defensible consumption baseline, and when is last year's history the wrong baseline for next year's system?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: USAGE_DATA_INTAKE gives the twelve-month reconstruction and anomaly handling, and LOAD_CHANGE_INTERROGATION gives the committed-versus-aspirational test that decides whether the baseline may be moved

competency_questions.question: How do I read this household's rate structure so the 'what you pay today' side of the comparison is the real bill and not a blended average?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TARIFF_STRUCTURE_READ names the rate-schedule components — fixed charges, tiers or time-of-use periods, minimum bills, riders — and explains which kWh are worth most to displace

competency_questions.question: How is exported energy compensated for a system interconnecting now, and what does that do to the value of building a bigger array?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXPORT_COMPENSATION_READ describes the compensation classes and the verify-in-your-jurisdiction rule, and SYSTEM_SIZING_LOGIC shows the regime deciding the offset target rather than the roof deciding it

competency_questions.question: How do I qualify a roof — planes, orientation, shade, remaining life — and which parts of that judgement are the installer's and not mine?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROOF_GEOMETRY_ASSESS produces usable area and orientation per plane, SHADE_ANALYSIS quantifies shade per plane and season, and ROOF_CONDITION_STRUCTURE separates the seller's early flag from the installer's engineering determination

competency_questions.question: What in the service equipment tells me a panel upgrade or a different connection method is likely, and how do I put that in the proposal before it becomes a change order?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ELECTRICAL_SERVICE_CHECK lists the observable signals and states the disclosure of the upgrade possibility as a decision path with installer-sourced pricing rather than a seller-invented figure

competency_questions.question: How do I present a production number as a model with uncertainty instead of a promise, and what would make any number a commitment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRODUCTION_MODELING names the model inputs, the stated loss assumptions and the band, and states that only a written guarantee from the party issuing it turns a modeled figure into a commitment

competency_questions.question: How do I size the array when consumption, roof area, export rules, panel capacity and budget all point at different answers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SYSTEM_SIZING_LOGIC states the offset target chosen, the constraint that bound it, and why the larger and smaller options were rejected

competency_questions.question: How do I build a savings comparison that still holds up when the homeowner checks it against their next twelve bills?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SAVINGS_MODEL_INTEGRITY reconstructs both sides of the bill the way the utility computes it including surviving fixed and non-bypassable charges, and ESCALATOR_HONESTY requires the zero-escalation case alongside any escalating case

competency_questions.question: What are the financing classes, who owns the system in each, and what must be disclosed before a homeowner signs one?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FINANCING_CLASS_LITERACY separates cash, loan, lease and power-purchase agreement by ownership, incentive entitlement, payment obligation and transfer at sale, and LOAN_MECHANICS_DISCLOSURE and LEASE_PPA_TERMS_DISCLOSURE give the disclosure content for each

competency_questions.question: How do I talk about tax credits, rebates and certificate programs without giving tax advice or booking them as money the homeowner is certain to get?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INCENTIVE_ELIGIBILITY_FRAMING treats each incentive as a class with eligibility conditions, names the publishing authority, routes eligibility to the homeowner's tax adviser, and flags program-closure risk

competency_questions.question: What actually happens between signature and the day the system is allowed to run, and how do I set that expectation without promising a date?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERMIT_INTERCONNECT_AWARENESS lays out the design, interconnection application, permit, install, inspection and permission-to-operate stages and requires timelines to be given as ranges with the current blocking stage named

competency_questions.question: How do I run an in-home appointment so consent is real — including with an elderly homeowner, a homeowner negotiating in a second language, or a household where one decision-maker is absent?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMER_PROTECTION_FRAME names the in-home solicitation and cancellation obligation classes with the verify-in-your-jurisdiction rule, and VULNERABLE_HOMEOWNER_CARE gives the pressure-free protocol and the walk-away rule

competency_questions.question: What is the last check that stops a defective proposal from reaching a signature, and what does the homeowner walk away holding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROPOSAL_ASSEMBLY_DISCLOSURE_PACK specifies the document contents and the ordering that puts obligations and uncertainties before the savings figure, and PRESIGNATURE_REVIEW_GATE gives the pass/stop audit items

glossary.definition: The compass direction a roof plane faces and the angle it rises at; together with latitude and shade they set how much of the available sunlight a plane can convert, and they are the first two facts recorded per candidate plane.

The share of the theoretically available annual irradiance a specific plane actually receives once obstructions are accounted for, measured on the roof with an instrument or modeled from imagery or LIDAR; it enters the production model as an input with its own uncertainty rather than as a comment.

A rate structure that prices energy differently by hour, day type and season, so the value of a displaced or exported kWh depends on when it happens; it is the reason a single blended cents-per-kWh figure misstates both the pre-solar and post-solar bill.

The rule set that decides what the utility credits for energy the array sends back to the grid — full retail netting, a reduced export rate or avoided-cost class, or a time-differentiated export value — together with its true-up period, surplus treatment and grandfathering terms; it varies by jurisdiction and utility and is revised often.

A component of the bill that a customer keeps paying on consumed energy regardless of how the array is credited; it is one of the reasons a post-solar bill does not fall to zero and must be carried into the comparison rather than netted away.

The utility's written authorization, issued after inspection and any meter work, that allows the installed system to be energized and to export; it is the true end of the process and the stage most often mistaken by homeowners for the install date.

The building or electrical department that issues the permit and performs inspection for the address; its plan-review and inspection queue is one of the timeline stages the seller does not control and must therefore describe as a range.

A third-party-ownership class in which the homeowner does not own the system and pays a price per kWh the system generates, as distinct from a lease where a fixed periodic payment is made for the use of the equipment; in both, incentives generally flow to the owner, not the resident.

A contractual clause that raises the homeowner's lease or power-purchase payment by a stated percentage each year of the term; it is separate from, and often confused with, the assumed rate of future utility price increases used on the do-nothing side of a comparison.

The mechanism by which a lender offering a below-market advertised rate is compensated: a charge to the dealer or seller that is embedded in the installed price, which is why identical hardware carries a different sticker under a low-rate loan than under cash; the size is a per-deal fact read from the lender's own schedule, never assumed.

nodes.definition: Fix, before any appointment is booked, the standing rule that every quantity a homeowner is shown must trace to one of three things — the homeowner's own utility data, the published tariff and interconnection rules of their utility, or a site-specific production model whose inputs are recorded — and that anything else is spoken as an open question rather than written as a claim. The charter also fixes the selling posture: no pricing that expires when the rep leaves the driveway, no fear framing built on invented rate-hike figures, no talk of never having a power bill again, and a standing invitation for the homeowner to have anyone they trust read the proposal. In a business paid per installed system, where the proposal is the only artifact the household keeps and shows their neighbours, this charter is the operating identity of the seller and the thing the whole subdomain is built to enforce.

included: the permitted-source rule for every shown quantity
the banned claim forms including guarantees of bill elimination and invented utility-inflation figures
the anti-pressure appointment posture and the standing third-party-review invitation
excluded: commission and clawback structure, which belongs to the market-models KB
installer selection and build quality, which belongs to the installer-partnership KB
any assertion about what a specific homeowner will save

pros.claim: A written charter turns 'sell ethically' into a rule a specific proposal either passes or fails, so it can be enforced by a checklist rather than by mood
pros.example: a rep who cannot name the artifact behind the monthly-savings line on page one deletes the line instead of defending it at the kitchen table

cons.claim: The charter loses deals in the room to competitors quoting flattering unverified numbers, and the loss is immediate while the reputation payoff is slow and invisible
cons.example: the neighbour signs the same week with a canvasser promising a guaranteed zero bill, and the honest proposal looks like the worse offer that evening

failure_modes: the charter is written but the proposal template is never rebuilt to match it, so the template keeps emitting unsourced savings claims
the charter is used as an objection-handling script instead of as a constraint on what the document may contain
the rep applies it to written material but reverts to guarantee language in conversation, where nothing is recorded
acceptance_tests: every numeric line in a sample proposal names the artifact it came from
no guarantee of a future bill, savings amount or utility rate appears in either the document or the appointment script
the third-party-review invitation is present in writing, not only spoken
revisit_triggers: a homeowner disputes a claim made in a proposal after install
a jurisdiction or utility publishes new marketing or savings-claim guidance for residential solar
a partner installer or lender supplies template material containing guarantee language

base.update_signal: an audit of post-install complaints showing which proposal claims actually generate disputes, or new advertising-claim guidance published by the regulator or utility in the operating territory

nodes.definition: Establish which classes of consumer-protection obligation attach to the way this business actually sells before the sales process is designed around them: in-home and door-to-door solicitation rules, written-contract and cancellation-notice requirements with their cooling-off periods, language-of-negotiation rules where a contract negotiated in one language must be delivered in it, savings-claim and advertising restrictions specific to residential solar, and any standalone disclosure document a jurisdiction requires to accompany a solar contract or a third-party-ownership agreement. The work is to identify the obligation classes that attach to the seller's own role, obtain the current text from the authority that publishes it, record the date it was checked, and verify current rules in your jurisdiction rather than transplanting a rule learned in another state or country. The seller's obligations are distinct from the installer's licensing and the lender's lending-disclosure obligations, and assuming someone else's paperwork covers yours is the classic error.

included: identifying which obligation classes attach to in-home solar selling in the operating jurisdiction
obtaining and dating the current authoritative text
routing questions that belong to the installer's licence or the lender's disclosures to their holder
excluded: legal advice or interpreting a specific contract for a homeowner
contractor licensing, bonding and workmanship obligations, which are the installer's
lender licensing and credit-application disclosures, which are the finance provider's

pros.claim: Knowing the obligation classes before the process is built means the required notices are part of the pack from the first appointment instead of being retrofitted after a dispute
pros.example: a jurisdiction with a home-solicitation cancellation-notice class makes that notice a fixed page of the pack rather than something a rep remembers to hand over

cons.claim: Obligation classes differ across jurisdiction lines and change without warning, so keeping current is unpaid overhead the commission does not fund
cons.example: a rep working both sides of a state line finds a standalone disclosure document required on one side with no counterpart on the other, and must maintain two packs

failure_modes: assuming a nationally distributed sales script is compliant everywhere it is used
treating the finance company's or installer's paperwork as satisfying the seller's own obligations
citing a specific rule from memory to a homeowner instead of naming the class and the authority
acceptance_tests: the applicable obligation classes are listed with the publishing authority named and a date of last verification
no jurisdiction-specific rule appears in client-facing material without a current-source check on file
the pack for each jurisdiction sold into is separately assembled and dated
revisit_triggers: the operator begins selling in a new jurisdiction or under a new utility
an enforcement action against a residential solar seller is reported in the market
a partner changes the contract or disclosure documents it supplies

base.update_signal: a published rule change, enforcement bulletin or consumer-protection advisory covering in-home solar sales in the operating jurisdiction, or entry into a new jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Keep, per household, a ledger pairing every input used in the proposal with the artifact it came from and the date it was captured: the bill images or the utility data export, the rate-schedule identifier, the export-rules page for the interconnection class, the shade model output or instrument readings, the service-panel photograph, the roof photographs, and the installer's own quoted price and scope. The ledger is what makes a proposal auditable a year later when the household compares its real bills to the estimate, and it is what turns a disagreement into a documented reconciliation instead of a credibility contest the seller loses by default. It is deliberately minimal — enough to defend every number and nothing more — because a seller has no business holding personal data the proposal does not need, and it is retained with the homeowner's knowledge.

included: capture and dating of the artifact behind every proposal input
rate-schedule and export-rule identifiers rather than remembered summaries
retention limited to what defends the proposal, held with the homeowner's knowledge
excluded: credit application and underwriting data, which stays with the finance provider
collecting household information the proposal does not use
the installer's as-built and commissioning records

pros.claim: An auditable proposal survives the post-install comparison, which is the moment that decides whether this household ever refers anyone
pros.example: when year-one output runs under the model, the shade file and the named weather dataset are on hand to explain the gap instead of the rep guessing in front of an angry customer

cons.claim: Capture discipline costs appointment time and homeowners resist handing over data before they trust the seller, so the ledger is thinnest exactly when the deal is earliest
cons.example: a homeowner who will not authorize a utility data download forces the estimate to be built from two bill images and labelled low-confidence throughout

failure_modes: screenshots kept without dates or rate-schedule identifiers, so the artifact cannot prove which tariff was in force
the ledger lives in a rep's personal phone and is gone when the rep leaves or the deal moves to another partner
capturing far more household data than the proposal needs, creating a liability with no benefit
acceptance_tests: every input on the proposal assumption page resolves to a dated artifact in the ledger
the tariff and export-rule artifacts carry the schedule identifier and the date they were retrieved
no data category is held that no proposal line depends on
revisit_triggers: a homeowner questions a number after install and the artifact cannot be produced
a partner installer or lender requests the basis of an estimate
the tariff or export rules change while the deal is still open

base.update_signal: a post-install dispute in which a missing artifact decided the outcome, or a change in what partners require as the documented basis of an estimate

nodes.definition: Build the household's consumption baseline from the strongest data it can supply: a full twelve months of billed kilowatt-hours, or the utility's interval or hourly export where the utility publishes one, rather than one summer bill annualized by a sales tool. The work is to reconstruct consumption month by month, to split it across rate periods where a time-of-use tariff applies, to flag anomalies — a vacant stretch, a failed pool pump, a genuinely unusual season, a meter estimate the utility later trued up — and to decide for each whether it is kept, adjusted or annotated. Where twelve months do not exist, because the household recently moved or the home is newly built, the baseline is labelled provisional throughout the proposal rather than quietly filled in from a regional average, because every downstream number inherits this one's error.

included: twelve-month kilowatt-hour reconstruction and time-of-use period splits
anomaly identification and the keep-adjust-annotate decision
explicit provisional labelling when history is short or missing
excluded: appliance-level energy audits and efficiency retrofit recommendations
gas or water consumption except where an electrification plan converts it into future electric load
judging the household's credit or ability to pay, which belongs to the finance provider

pros.claim: A full-year baseline kills the seasonal-extrapolation error that produces the most common oversized system
pros.example: annualizing an August bill in a cooling-dominated climate can imply a system far larger than the household's real annual use, which then overproduces into a weak export credit

cons.claim: Twelve months is often simply unavailable, and the honest response — a provisional baseline — makes the proposal look weaker than a competitor's confident fabrication
cons.example: a family four months into a new build has no representative history at all, and the competitor's proposal shows a precise savings figure anyway

failure_modes: using the dollar amount instead of kilowatt-hours, so a mid-year rate change contaminates the baseline
silently substituting a regional average for missing months without labelling it
ignoring the time-of-use period split on a tariff where the split is the whole story
acceptance_tests: twelve months of kilowatt-hours are present or the baseline is labelled provisional on every page that uses it
each anomalous month carries a keep, adjust or annotate decision with a reason
the baseline is expressed in kilowatt-hours, with dollars derived from the tariff rather than the reverse
revisit_triggers: a further billing period arrives that contradicts the assumed baseline
the homeowner discloses an occupancy change during the baseline year
the utility restates or trues up an estimated read

base.update_signal: post-install comparisons of actual consumption against the baseline used, showing which reconstruction shortcuts produce the largest errors

nodes.definition: Interrogate, before the baseline is used for sizing, every way next year's consumption will differ from last year's: an electric vehicle arriving or leaving, a heat pump replacing gas or resistance heat, a pool or spa, a planned addition or accessory dwelling, a home-office change, an occupant joining or leaving the household, or an efficiency project already contracted. Each candidate change is classified as committed — ordered, financed, permitted or already installed — or aspirational, and only committed changes are allowed to move the baseline. Aspirational changes are shown as a labelled sensitivity beside the base case, and the homeowner is told plainly that a system sized for a vehicle they have not bought overproduces until they buy it, which under a weak export-compensation regime is a direct loss they carry, not the seller.

included: the structured forward-load interview across electrification, occupancy and building changes
the committed-versus-aspirational classification test
presenting aspirational load as a labelled sensitivity rather than as baseline
excluded: designing the household's electrification plan or specifying heat-pump or charger equipment
guaranteeing that a future load will materialize
battery sizing, which follows from tariff and resilience goals outside this KB

pros.claim: The committed test stops the most flattering oversizing story a seller can tell themselves, which is that the customer will grow into it
pros.example: a homeowner who says they will probably get an electric car someday gets a base-case system sized to today's use plus a clearly labelled larger option, not a silently upsized array

cons.claim: Refusing to size for aspirational load can undersize a household that genuinely does electrify soon, and adding capacity later is rarely a simple bolt-on
cons.example: a household that installs a heat pump the following winter finds that adding modules means a new interconnection application and possibly a service upgrade

failure_modes: counting a homeowner's enthusiasm as a commitment because it justifies a bigger array
missing an occupant departure — a child leaving for university — that will lower consumption
treating an efficiency retrofit already under contract as if consumption will stay flat
acceptance_tests: each declared future load carries a committed or aspirational classification with the evidence named
the base case uses committed loads only and any aspirational case is separately labelled
revisit_triggers: the homeowner commits to a load change while the proposal is still open
an efficiency or electrification project completes before interconnection

base.update_signal: follow-up on past deals showing how often declared aspirational loads actually arrived, which recalibrates how much weight an intention deserves

nodes.definition: Read the household's actual rate schedule as a mechanism rather than as an average price: which fixed customer or service charges are payable regardless of consumption, whether energy is priced in consumption tiers or by time-of-use period, whether a minimum bill or minimum delivery charge sets a floor, which riders, surcharges and taxes attach and how they scale, and — on the minority of residential schedules that carry one — any demand component that prices the household's peak draw. This determines which kilowatt-hours are worth most to displace and what the bill cannot fall below no matter how much the array produces. It is also the reason a proposal that reduces the whole tariff to one blended cents-per-kilowatt-hour figure is usually wrong on both the before and the after side, and why the schedule identifier and its effective date belong in the evidence ledger.

included: identifying the household's actual rate schedule and its components
which charges survive regardless of production and which are displaceable
whether a tariff change is mandatory or optional on interconnection
excluded: advising the homeowner which rate schedule to elect, which is a decision for them with the utility
gas tariffs except where electrification moves load between fuels
wholesale market or utility ratemaking analysis

pros.claim: Reading the schedule reveals the floor under the bill, so the proposal never implies a bill can go to zero when fixed and minimum charges make that impossible
pros.example: a household on a schedule with a monthly customer charge and a minimum delivery charge keeps paying those every month even in a high-production summer

cons.claim: Rate schedules are long, cross-referenced and revised, and reading one properly costs time on every deal, including the ones that never close
cons.example: a utility with several residential schedules plus solar-specific ones forces a per-household determination of which schedule applies before and after interconnection

failure_modes: using a blended average rate for both sides of the comparison
missing that interconnecting mandates a move to a different rate schedule with different period definitions
ignoring riders and taxes that scale with consumption and therefore change with production
acceptance_tests: the schedule identifier and effective date are recorded in the ledger
the fixed, minimum and non-bypassable components are listed separately from displaceable energy charges
any mandatory schedule change on interconnection is identified before the savings model is built
revisit_triggers: the utility files or implements a rate change while the deal is open
the household is moved to a different schedule by the utility
a tariff component the model relied on is restructured

base.update_signal: a published tariff revision or a solar-specific schedule change in the operating utility's territory, or a homeowner bill that does not reconcile to the schedule as read

nodes.definition: Determine how energy the array sends back to the grid is compensated under the rules that will be in force for a system interconnecting now, not the rules a neighbour got years ago: the full-retail netting class, the reduced export-rate or avoided-cost class, time-differentiated export values that make an afternoon-facing array worth more or less than a morning-facing one, the true-up period and what happens to a surplus credit at true-up, the charges that survive netting, and whether an existing customer's grandfathered terms carry over or are forfeited on a system change. This is class-level knowledge only; verify current rules in your jurisdiction and with the specific utility, because these regimes are revised frequently and often with a cutover date, and a proposal built on the outgoing regime overstates the value of every exported kilowatt-hour it counts.

included: identifying the compensation class applicable to a system interconnecting now
true-up, surplus and grandfathering treatment
how export value differs by hour where the regime is time-differentiated
excluded: predicting future regulatory changes as if they were known
advising on whether to rush a filing to beat a cutover, which is a decision for the homeowner with the facts stated
the interconnection application itself, which is the installer's filing

pros.claim: The export regime, not the roof, is what makes surplus generation worth building, so reading it first prevents a whole class of confidently oversized proposals
pros.example: under a reduced export-rate class, the last increment of an oversized array earns far less per kilowatt-hour than the household pays for the energy it displaces, which changes the honest recommendation

cons.claim: Regimes change mid-deal and cutover dates create pressure to hurry a homeowner, which is exactly the pressure this business must not apply
cons.example: a pending regime change gives every seller in the territory a deadline story, and the honest version of it is a stated fact with a source rather than a countdown clock

failure_modes: modeling exports at retail value under a regime that credits them at a lower export rate
assuming a neighbour's grandfathered terms apply to this household
ignoring that adding capacity later can move an existing customer onto the current regime
acceptance_tests: the applicable compensation class is named with the source page and retrieval date in the ledger
the model values exported and self-consumed energy separately rather than at one rate
any grandfathering or cutover claim is sourced to the utility or regulator, not to sales material
revisit_triggers: the regulator or utility announces or implements a change to export compensation
the deal remains open across an announced cutover date
the homeowner already has an existing system whose terms may be affected

base.update_signal: a regulatory decision, tariff filing or utility bulletin changing export compensation or grandfathering in the operating territory

nodes.definition: Segment the roof into candidate planes and record for each the azimuth, pitch, dimensions, covering material and the deductions that shrink usable area: vents, stacks, skylights, hips and valleys, existing equipment, fire-code setback and access-pathway classes that differ by jurisdiction, and any homeowner-association, historic-district or local aesthetic restriction the household mentions. The output is a usable-area and orientation picture good enough to model production and to tell the household early and plainly which planes cannot carry modules and why, so the conversation about a smaller-than-hoped array happens at the first appointment rather than after the installer's site audit. Structural adequacy, attachment method and racking layout remain the installer's engineering determination; this unit produces the survey they will check, not the design.

included: plane segmentation with azimuth, pitch and dimensions
usable-area deductions including setback and pathway classes and obstructions
recording association or historic restrictions the household discloses
excluded: structural, attachment and racking design, which is the installer's engineering
final code interpretation of setback and pathway rules, which is the authority having jurisdiction's
roof measurement presented as a construction drawing

pros.claim: Early plane-by-plane truth prevents the proposal from selling area that fire pathways, obstructions or an association rule will not allow
pros.example: a large south plane that turns out to be mostly setback and vent deduction supports far fewer modules than a satellite-image sales tool suggested

cons.claim: A careful survey costs appointment time and can only be approximate without roof access, so it must be labelled as a survey subject to the installer's site audit
cons.example: a steep tile roof cannot be safely walked by a seller, leaving dimensions estimated from imagery with a stated tolerance

failure_modes: treating a satellite outline as usable area without deducting obstructions and pathways
recording one azimuth for a roof that actually has several planes at different orientations
not asking about association or historic restrictions until after signature
acceptance_tests: each candidate plane has azimuth, pitch, gross and usable area with the deductions itemized
the survey is labelled as subject to the installer's site audit and engineering
disclosed association or historic restrictions are recorded in the ledger
revisit_triggers: the installer's site audit returns different usable area
the household discloses a restriction after the survey
a planned roof change alters the available planes

base.update_signal: systematic differences between seller surveys and installer site audits on usable area, or a change in local setback and access-pathway requirements

nodes.definition: Quantify shading on each candidate plane across the whole year instead of eyeballing the roof at two in the afternoon in June: remote modeling from imagery or LIDAR where that data is good, on-roof instrument measurement where it is not, plus the judgements neither method captures — a neighbour's tree that will be substantially taller in a decade, a vacant lot next door zoned for two storeys, a chimney that shades exactly the part of the array that carries the string. Shade is recorded per plane and per season and carried into the production model as an input with its own uncertainty rather than as a comment in the notes, and heavily shaded planes are either dropped from the design or flagged to the installer for module-level electronics, with the effect on cost stated rather than absorbed silently.

included: per-plane, per-season shade quantification by remote model or on-roof instrument
future-shade judgement for growing vegetation and permitted construction
flagging planes that need module-level electronics or should be dropped
excluded: string design and electronics selection, which is the installer's
advising a homeowner to remove a neighbour's tree or asserting any right to light
guaranteeing that future shade will not change

pros.claim: Measured shade is the single input most able to break a production estimate, so quantifying it converts the largest source of post-install disappointment into a stated uncertainty
pros.example: a plane that looks clear in a midday photo is shaded by a neighbour's oak for the low-sun winter hours that a heating-dominated household most needs

cons.claim: Instrument measurement means roof access, time and sometimes a second visit, and remote modeling is only as good as the imagery and vegetation data behind it
cons.example: recent imagery that predates a fast-growing tree line makes a remote shade model look better than the roof actually is

failure_modes: assessing shade only at the season and hour of the visit
averaging shade across the whole roof instead of recording it per plane
ignoring predictable future shade because it is inconvenient to raise
acceptance_tests: shade is recorded per plane with the method named and the output stored in the ledger
seasonal variation is represented rather than a single annual figure
future-shade risks the household disclosed or the survey observed are written into the proposal
revisit_triggers: vegetation is removed or added at the property or a neighbour's
the installer's site audit disagrees materially with the shade model
year-one production runs below the modeled band

base.update_signal: comparisons of modeled versus monitored output on past installs grouped by shade method, showing where remote modeling systematically flatters a site

nodes.definition: Assess whether this roof should carry an array for the next couple of decades at all: covering type and approximate remaining life, visible damage or prior repair, how many layers are already there, sagging or deflection visible from the ground or the attic, penetrations, and access. The decision to re-roof before installation or to install now and pay for a removal and reinstallation later is put to the household as an explicit cost-and-timing trade whose numbers come from a roofer's quote and the installer's own removal-and-reinstall pricing, never from a figure the seller invents to make either option look better. Structural adequacy is the installer's and their engineer's determination; the seller's job is to raise the question early enough that it never surfaces as a change order after signature, because that is the moment a household stops trusting everything else in the proposal.

included: remaining-life and condition observation with photographs
presenting the re-roof-now versus remove-and-reinstall-later trade with sourced numbers
escalating structural doubt to the installer before design proceeds
excluded: structural engineering determinations and load calculations
quoting roofing work or acting as a roofing contractor
warranting the roof's remaining life

pros.claim: Raising roof life before financing paperwork keeps the household's options open, since bundling or sequencing a re-roof is far cheaper to decide before a loan is documented than after
pros.example: a covering near the end of its life is best replaced before install, and the household can only weigh that if the removal-and-reinstall cost is on the table early

cons.claim: Raising it can kill or delay the deal outright, and the seller carries that cost while the benefit lands with the household and the installer
cons.example: a household told their roof should be replaced first postpones the whole project a year, and the commission with it

failure_modes: staying quiet about an aging roof to protect the deal
quoting a re-roof cost from memory instead of from a roofer's quote
treating a visible sag as cosmetic rather than escalating it to the installer
acceptance_tests: roof covering type, observed condition and approximate remaining life are recorded with photographs
where remaining life is short, the re-roof-now versus reinstall-later trade appears in the proposal with sourced numbers
any structural concern is escalated to the installer in writing before design
revisit_triggers: the installer's site audit or the roofer disagrees with the observed condition
the household obtains a roofing quote that changes the trade
a storm or leak occurs before install

base.update_signal: how often installer site audits or later leaks reveal roof conditions the seller's walkthrough missed, and which observable signals predicted them

nodes.definition: Photograph and read the service equipment at the first opportunity: main breaker rating, busbar rating and the label that states it, panel make and any known defect or recall class, available breaker spaces, meter location and service type, and any subpanel arrangement the array might land on. The screen produces an early probability that a panel upgrade, a derate, a line-side or supply-side connection, or a meter relocation will be needed — one of the most common reasons a price moves between the proposal and the signed contract — so the possibility is disclosed up front as a decision path with installer-sourced pricing rather than discovered by the installer's site auditor after the household has told their family they are going solar. Code interpretation and the final connection method belong to the installer's licensed electrician and the authority having jurisdiction.

included: service-equipment photography and rating capture
early probability that an upgrade or alternative connection method is required
disclosing that possibility with a decision path and installer-sourced cost
excluded: code interpretation and connection-method selection, which is the installer's electrician's and the authority's
performing or pricing electrical work
load calculations that require licensed judgement

pros.claim: A photographed panel label turns the most common post-signature price surprise into a disclosed possibility, which is the difference between a change order and a betrayal
pros.example: a panel whose busbar rating leaves no room for the interconnection under the applicable rule means an upgrade or a supply-side connection, and the household should learn that in week one

cons.claim: The screen is a probability, not a determination, and stating it as a range can read as evasive to a household that wants one number
cons.example: a homeowner asks whether they need a panel upgrade and the honest answer is that the installer's electrician will determine it, with the likely cost path stated in advance

failure_modes: recording the main breaker rating but not the busbar rating printed on the label
omitting the upgrade possibility from the proposal because it weakens the price
assuming a subpanel can host the interconnection without the electrician's review
acceptance_tests: clear photographs of the service panel, its label and the meter are in the ledger
the proposal states whether a service upgrade or alternative connection is possible and how its cost would be determined
no connection method is asserted as decided before the installer's electrician reviews it
revisit_triggers: the installer's site audit finds different service conditions
the household adds load that changes the service calculation
the utility or authority changes interconnection requirements for existing services

base.update_signal: the rate at which installer site audits overturn the seller's service screen, and any change in interconnection or panel-rating requirements in the territory

nodes.definition: Produce a modeled estimate of annual and monthly generation for the specified array from the plane geometry, the measured shade inputs, the module and inverter characteristics the installer will actually use, and a named long-run weather dataset, with the loss assumptions — soiling, wiring and mismatch, inverter efficiency, availability, and degradation across the term — stated on the page rather than buried in a tool default. The estimate is presented as a central model output with a band around it and an explicit statement that individual weather years vary, and the tool, its version and every input are recorded in the evidence ledger so the estimate can be reconstructed later. A production estimate is a model, not a promise: only a written guarantee issued by the party that stands behind it — an installer, a manufacturer or a third-party owner under its own agreement — turns any number into a commitment, and the seller never converts one into the other by tone of voice.

included: modeled annual and monthly generation with stated losses and a band
naming the weather dataset, tool and version in the ledger
the modeled-not-promised framing and where a real guarantee would come from
excluded: issuing any production guarantee, which only the party standing behind it may do
final equipment selection and string design, which is the installer's
monitoring and post-install performance claims analysis, which follows install

pros.claim: Stating the losses and the band on the page is what lets a year-one shortfall be explained rather than denied, which preserves the referral that is this business's only durable asset
pros.example: a low-irradiance first year lands inside a stated band and the conversation is about weather variance instead of about whether the seller lied

cons.claim: A band looks weaker than a competitor's single confident number, and homeowners frequently read uncertainty as incompetence rather than honesty
cons.example: two proposals show similar central estimates but the one with a range beside it reads as the less capable company

failure_modes: shipping tool defaults for soiling and degradation as if they were site facts
presenting a single figure with no band and letting the homeowner hear it as a floor
modeling a different module or inverter than the installer will actually fit
acceptance_tests: the proposal names the modeling tool, the weather dataset and every loss assumption used
production appears as a central estimate with a band and a weather-variance statement
the words used for the estimate contain no guarantee, and any real guarantee is attributed to its issuer
revisit_triggers: the installer changes module or inverter selection
shade or geometry inputs are revised by the site audit
monitored output on comparable installs diverges from the model

base.update_signal: monitored first-year output from past installs compared against the model that sold them, broken down by shade method and loss assumptions

nodes.definition: Choose the array size at the point where five constraints disagree: the consumption baseline plus committed load changes, the usable roof area and the orientation quality of what is left, the export-compensation regime that decides what surplus generation is actually worth, the service-equipment capacity that decides what can be interconnected without an upgrade, and the household's budget or financing capacity. The unit of work is the explicit trade — an offset target chosen and written down, with the binding constraint named and the reasons the larger and the smaller options were rejected — rather than the default of filling the roof. Where compensation for surplus is weak, sizing to consumption rather than to area is usually the honest recommendation even though it directly reduces the commission on the deal, and that is precisely the decision this business's reputation is made of.

included: the offset-target decision with the binding constraint named
documented rejection reasons for the larger and smaller options
the honest-undersizing recommendation where export value is weak
excluded: electrical design, string sizing and equipment layout, which are the installer's
storage sizing beyond noting where it changes the export arithmetic
promising a specific offset percentage as an outcome

pros.claim: Naming the binding constraint makes the size defensible to a household that will later ask why the array is not bigger, and defensible to the seller's own conscience when the commission argues the other way
pros.example: an array bound by usable area after pathway deductions is explained by the roof, not by a preference, and the household can see the deduction itemization

cons.claim: A smaller right-sized system pays less and can lose to a competitor's larger proposal that the household reads as more generous
cons.example: a competing proposal fills the roof and shows a bigger savings headline that quietly depends on exporting surplus at a value the regime does not pay

failure_modes: sizing to the roof because the roof is the easiest constraint to see
sizing to an aspirational load the household never commits to
hiding the fact that a service upgrade is what actually capped the size
acceptance_tests: the proposal states the offset target, the binding constraint and why a larger and a smaller option were rejected
surplus generation is valued under the applicable export class rather than at retail
any size driven by a service-capacity limit says so plainly
revisit_triggers: a load commitment changes after sizing
the site audit changes usable area or service capacity
the export regime changes while the deal is open

base.update_signal: follow-up on installed systems showing how often the delivered offset matched the target and which constraint was misjudged when it did not

nodes.definition: Construct the before-and-after comparison the way the utility actually computes a bill rather than as a subtraction of two averages: apply the household's real rate schedule to its real baseline for the do-nothing side; for the with-solar side apply modeled generation against consumption under the correct netting or export-credit rules, keep the fixed charges, minimum bills, non-bypassable components and taxes that survive, and only then subtract or add the financing payment where a payment exists. Savings are expressed as a modeled range with every assumption listed on the same page as the number, and the first-year figure is kept separate from any lifetime figure so that a large lifetime total cannot smuggle in an unstated escalation assumption. The model is built so that it can be reconciled line by line against the household's next twelve real bills, because that reconciliation is exactly what will happen.

included: tariff-faithful reconstruction of both sides of the bill
retention of fixed, minimum and non-bypassable charges in the with-solar case
separating first-year from lifetime figures and listing assumptions beside the number
excluded: any statement that a specific saving will occur
return-on-investment advice or investment comparison, which is financial advice
tax treatment of savings or incentives, which belongs to the household's adviser

pros.claim: A tariff-faithful model can be reconciled against real bills, which converts the twelve-month post-install audit from a threat into the seller's best referral event
pros.example: a household that sees the residual fixed charge in the model and then on their real bill concludes the seller told them the truth about everything else too

cons.claim: Doing it properly produces a smaller headline than a blended-rate subtraction, and it costs real modeling time on every deal including the ones that never sign
cons.example: keeping minimum bills and non-bypassable charges in the with-solar case visibly shrinks the monthly saving compared with a competitor's simpler arithmetic

failure_modes: netting away charges that survive netting so the modeled bill falls near zero
presenting a lifetime savings total whose escalation assumption is not on the page
comparing a with-solar bill that excludes the financing payment against a do-nothing bill that includes everything
acceptance_tests: the with-solar case retains every charge that survives under the applicable tariff and export class
the financing payment is included in the with-solar case wherever one exists
first-year and lifetime figures are separated and each carries its assumptions on the same page
revisit_triggers: the tariff, export regime or system size changes before signature
the household's real bills after install do not reconcile to the model
the financing product or payment changes

base.update_signal: line-by-line reconciliation of past customers' real post-install bills against the model that sold them, identifying which components the model routinely got wrong

nodes.definition: Handle the two escalation numbers that quietly decide whether a solar proposal looks extraordinary or ordinary. The first is the assumed rate of future utility price increase applied to the do-nothing side of the comparison, which compounds across a twenty-plus-year horizon and can manufacture almost any lifetime savings figure a seller wants; it must be sourced to the utility's own published rate history or a regulator's filing, shown alongside a zero-escalation case, and never presented as a forecast the seller can make. The second is the contractual escalator inside a lease or power-purchase agreement, which raises the household's own payment every year of the term; it is stated in the first minute of that conversation, with the arithmetic of what the payment becomes late in the term shown explicitly, rather than left to be discovered in the document or after signature.

included: sourcing any utility-escalation assumption and pairing it with a zero-escalation case
stating a contractual escalator early with its late-term arithmetic
keeping the two escalation concepts explicitly distinct for the household
excluded: forecasting future energy prices as if the seller could
advising whether an escalating agreement is a good deal for this household
modeling inflation or investment alternatives, which is financial advice

pros.claim: Showing the zero-escalation case removes the single largest lever for manufacturing a savings story and makes the proposal robust to a homeowner's own scepticism
pros.example: a household that distrusts any assumption about future rates can read the proposal at zero escalation and still see whether the deal stands up

cons.claim: The zero-escalation case makes the honest proposal look materially less attractive than a competitor's compounding forecast, and the difference is largest exactly where lifetime totals are quoted
cons.example: a lifetime savings figure built on an aggressive compounding assumption dwarfs the same system's zero-escalation figure, and the household sees two numbers with no way to referee them

failure_modes: conflating the utility escalation assumption with the contract escalator so the household hears one number
quoting a rate-increase assumption from sales material with no source
leaving the late-term payment under an escalating agreement uncalculated
acceptance_tests: any utility-escalation assumption names its source and appears beside a zero-escalation case
any contractual escalator is stated with the resulting payment shown at the late-term point
the two escalation concepts are labelled distinctly wherever both appear
revisit_triggers: the utility files or implements a rate change
the third-party-ownership product changes its escalator
the household asks for a lifetime figure not previously modeled

base.update_signal: the operating utility's published multi-year rate history and any regulator-filed forecast, plus complaint patterns from households whose escalating payments outran their bill savings

nodes.definition: Be able to explain, before any pricing conversation begins, the structural difference between the financing classes: cash purchase, a secured or unsecured consumer loan, a lease, and a power-purchase agreement. For each class the operator must state who owns the equipment, who is entitled to claim any incentive attached to ownership, what the household's payment obligation actually is — debt service, a rent for equipment, or a price per kilowatt-hour generated — who is responsible for maintenance, monitoring and eventual inverter replacement, what happens at the end of the term, and what happens when the home is sold. This is structural education delivered before price, because the class determines what the household is agreeing to for decades; which class suits a given household is a decision for them with their own financial or tax adviser, and the seller states the structures without steering toward the one that pays the most.

included: the ownership, incentive-entitlement, obligation, maintenance, end-of-term and transfer-at-sale profile of each class
delivering the class comparison before price
stating the classes without steering by seller compensation
excluded: recommending a class for a specific household, which is their decision with their adviser
credit underwriting and application handling, which belongs to the finance provider
commission differences between products, which belongs to the market-models KB

pros.claim: Teaching the classes before price gives the household a frame to evaluate everything that follows, and it is the cheapest possible protection against the regret that drives this industry's complaint volume
pros.example: a household that understands that under third-party ownership they do not own the system and do not claim owner incentives will not later feel a credit was taken from them

cons.claim: The structural conversation lengthens the appointment and can move a household toward the class that pays the seller least
cons.example: a household that came in wanting the lowest monthly payment leaves choosing cash after understanding the transfer-at-sale complications of a long third-party agreement

failure_modes: presenting the classes as monthly payments rather than as different things being bought
letting the product with the best seller compensation frame the comparison
answering an eligibility question that belongs to the household's tax adviser
acceptance_tests: the household can restate who will own the system and what the payment obligation is under the class they chose
the class comparison was delivered before a price was presented
every eligibility question raised is routed to the household's own adviser with that routing recorded
revisit_triggers: the household's circumstances change in a way that changes what a class means for them
a partner introduces or withdraws a financing product
a disclosure obligation class attaching to a product changes

base.update_signal: complaint and cancellation patterns by financing class, and changes in the products partners actually offer in this market

nodes.definition: Disclose how a solar loan is actually built before a household signs one. Lenders offering below-market advertised rates are typically compensated by a fee charged to the dealer and embedded in the installed price, which is why identical hardware carries a different sticker under a low-rate loan than under cash — the size of that fee is a per-deal fact read from the lender's own schedule and the installer's pricing, never a figure the seller assumes or invents. Many products are also structured with a lower initial payment on the assumption that a lump sum, typically an expected tax credit, is applied to principal by a set date, and the payment re-amortizes upward if it is not. The disclosure covers the term, the interest treatment, prepayment terms, whether the loan is secured against the property or by a fixture filing, what happens on sale of the home, and where in the lender's own documents each of these is written. Whether this household will actually receive any credit is a question for their tax adviser, not an assumption the seller may build a payment around.

included: the dealer-fee mechanism and why price differs by product
the step-payment and re-amortization structure and what triggers it
term, prepayment, security interest and sale-of-home treatment, pointed to the lender's own documents
excluded: advising which loan product a household should choose
predicting whether a household will receive an incentive, which is their tax adviser's question
the lender's underwriting, application and adverse-action process

pros.claim: Explaining the step payment before signature prevents the single most common financing complaint in this industry, which arrives eighteen months later when the payment jumps
pros.example: a household that could not use the expected credit sees the higher re-amortized payment coming because the seller showed both payment levels at the table

cons.claim: Explaining the dealer-fee mechanism invites an uncomfortable price comparison against the cash option and can stall a deal at the moment of decision
cons.example: a household asked to compare the cash price with the financed price starts negotiating the difference rather than choosing a product

failure_modes: quoting the low initial payment as the payment
assuming the household has the tax appetite the loan structure presumes
describing the security interest from memory rather than from the lender's document
acceptance_tests: both the initial and the re-amortized payment are shown, with the trigger and the deadline stated
the existence of an embedded finance cost and its effect on the price comparison is stated
every loan term cited points to the page in the lender's document where it appears
revisit_triggers: the lender changes product terms or fee schedule
the household's expected incentive position changes
the household indicates they may sell the home during the term

base.update_signal: lender product-term updates and the observed frequency of re-amortization complaints among past customers of each product

nodes.definition: Walk the terms of a third-party-ownership agreement that determine what the household has actually agreed to, and do it before price rather than after: the term length, the escalator, whether the payment is a fixed periodic amount for the equipment or a price per kilowatt-hour the system generates, any production guarantee and the true-up mechanism that backs it, who performs and pays for maintenance, monitoring and inverter replacement, insurance and damage responsibilities, the end-of-term options, the buyout and how it is calculated, and — the term that surfaces years later at the worst moment — the transfer process at sale of the home, including whether the buyer must qualify, what happens if they will not assume, and what filing is recorded against the property. This is where regret in residential solar concentrates, so the walk-through is a fixed script covering every one of those terms with the agreement open, not a summary.

included: term, escalator, payment basis, guarantee and true-up, maintenance and insurance responsibility
end-of-term options, buyout mechanism and transfer-at-sale process including any recorded filing
delivering the walk-through with the agreement open, before price
excluded: advising whether a third-party agreement suits this household
interpreting the contract as legal advice or predicting how a clause would be enforced
the third-party owner's own credit and eligibility decisions

pros.claim: A scripted walk-through of transfer-at-sale and buyout defuses the failure that damages this vertical's reputation most, which is a household discovering the agreement only when they try to sell the house
pros.example: a household planning to move within a few years learns before signing that a buyer must qualify to assume the agreement or the seller must arrange a buyout

cons.claim: The full walk-through is long, and delivering it before price sometimes ends the conversation in the room where a shorter version would have closed
cons.example: a household that hears the escalator and the transfer conditions up front decides to save toward a cash purchase instead

failure_modes: summarizing the agreement instead of walking the terms with the document open
presenting only the first-year payment on an escalating agreement
leaving transfer-at-sale and the recorded filing unmentioned because the household did not ask
acceptance_tests: every term in the walk-through script is covered with the agreement open and the coverage recorded
the household can restate the term length, the escalator and what happens if they sell the home
the buyout mechanism and any recorded filing are stated in the proposal pack
revisit_triggers: the third-party owner revises its agreement
the household's plans to move or refinance change
a disclosure obligation class attaching to third-party ownership changes in the jurisdiction

base.update_signal: agreement revisions from third-party owners and the pattern of complaints arising at home sale among past third-party-ownership customers

nodes.definition: Frame incentives — tax credits, utility or state rebates, performance-based or certificate-style programs, and property or sales tax treatments — as classes with eligibility conditions and expiry risk, never as money this household is certain to receive. The operator explains the mechanism: who is entitled to claim it, whether it is a credit against a tax liability rather than a payment, whether it flows to the owner of the equipment which under a lease or power-purchase agreement is not the resident, whether program funds are capped, queued or reserved at application, and what date or milestone governs. The publishing authority is named, the retrieval date is recorded, and every eligibility question is routed to the household's own tax adviser. Verify current program status in your jurisdiction before relying on any of it, because incentive rules are revised and closed on short notice, and a proposal whose savings depend on a program that closes before interconnection was never honest to begin with.

included: incentive classes, their claiming party and their mechanism
naming the publishing authority and recording the retrieval date
routing eligibility questions to the household's tax adviser and flagging program-closure risk
excluded: telling a household whether they qualify or how much they will receive, which is tax advice
filing or claiming on the household's behalf
treating an incentive as a certainty inside the savings model

pros.claim: Framing incentives as conditional keeps the savings model honest and protects the household from building a payment structure on money that may not arrive
pros.example: a retired household with little tax liability learns that a credit against tax is not the same as a payment before choosing a loan whose payment step assumes it

cons.claim: Conditional framing weakens the headline and is easy for a competitor to beat by simply stating the incentive as a discount
cons.example: a competing proposal shows the incentive subtracted from the price as if it were already received, and looks cheaper on the page

failure_modes: subtracting a tax credit from the price as though it were a rebate at purchase
assuming an owner incentive applies under a third-party-ownership structure
citing a program from memory after its terms or funding have changed
acceptance_tests: each incentive named carries its claiming party, its mechanism, its authority and a retrieval date
no incentive is netted into the price or the savings model as if it were certain
the adviser-referral wording appears wherever eligibility is discussed
revisit_triggers: a program's rules, funding or deadlines change
the household changes financing class in a way that changes who claims
the deal remains open past a program milestone

base.update_signal: program bulletins from the publishing authority showing rule, funding or deadline changes, and cases where a household could not use an incentive the proposal had assumed

nodes.definition: Know the sequence between signature and switch-on well enough to set expectations honestly: design and engineering, the utility interconnection application and its approval, the building and electrical permit from the authority having jurisdiction plus any association or historic approval, installation, inspection and any re-inspection after corrections, utility meter work where required, and finally permission to operate before the system may legally run and export. Each stage sits in a queue the seller does not control, so timelines are given as ranges based on current local experience with the blocking stage named, and no completion or switch-on date is ever promised. The applications, drawings and code compliance are the installer's responsibility; the seller's contribution is accurate expectation-setting, never contradicting the installer's own schedule, and making sure the household knows that an installed array on the roof is not yet a system they are allowed to use.

included: the stage sequence from design to permission to operate
timeline communication as ranges with the blocking stage named
explaining that installation is not authorization to operate
excluded: preparing or filing permit and interconnection applications, which is the installer's
code compliance and plan-set design
post-install schedule management and escalation, which belongs to the installer-partnership KB

pros.claim: Staged range-based expectations absorb the queue variance that otherwise turns a satisfied buyer into an angry one during the silent weeks after install
pros.example: a household told that inspection and utility authorization follow installation is not surprised when panels sit dark on the roof for weeks

cons.claim: Honest ranges are wide, and a household comparing proposals often reads the seller quoting a confident date as the more organized company
cons.example: a competitor promises a specific switch-on date that no queue can guarantee, and wins the comparison in the room

failure_modes: quoting an install or switch-on date the installer never committed to
omitting the authorization stage so the household expects to use the system on install day
repeating a stale queue estimate after local conditions have changed
acceptance_tests: the proposal shows the stages in order with ranges rather than dates and names the current blocking stage
the distinction between installation and permission to operate is stated in writing
no timeline in the pack contradicts what the installer has committed to
revisit_triggers: the authority or the utility changes its process or its queue lengthens
the installer changes its scheduling commitments
an association or historic approval is added to the path

base.update_signal: observed elapsed times by stage on recent local projects, and any published process change by the authority having jurisdiction or the utility

nodes.definition: Run the appointment so that consent is real rather than merely obtained. No offer that expires when the rep leaves the driveway, no signature at a first visit where the household asks for time, an explicit invitation for a spouse, adult child or adviser to be present or to review afterwards, and the full materials left behind whether or not anything is signed. Where there are signs that a homeowner may not be in a position to evaluate a decades-long agreement — apparent cognitive difficulty, a language of negotiation the rep does not share, a household member answering for someone who is not tracking the conversation, or an owner who cannot restate the payment obligation in their own words — the protocol is to stop, arrange a competent interpreter or an independent trusted party rather than an improvising family member or a child, and to walk away from any deal that can only be closed by pressure. A signature obtained from someone who cannot restate what they signed is the most expensive thing this business can produce, because it becomes a cancellation, a complaint, and a story the whole neighbourhood hears.

included: the no-expiring-offer and leave-materials rules
the restate-in-your-own-words comprehension check and the interpreter or trusted-party path
the explicit walk-away rule for deals closable only by pressure
excluded: assessing capacity clinically or making any determination about a person's competence
acting as an interpreter, adviser or advocate for the household
the household's internal decision-making about who signs

pros.claim: A comprehension check catches the deals that would have cancelled or complained anyway, and it does so before the household, the installer and the seller have all spent money
pros.example: a homeowner who cannot restate the escalator in their own words reveals a misunderstanding that would have surfaced years later as an accusation of deception

cons.claim: Slowing down loses deals to whoever knocks next, and the cost of walking away is immediate, personal and unshared
cons.example: a rep who declines to close in a household without an interpreter watches a competitor sign the same household the following week

failure_modes: using a child or a passing neighbour as an interpreter for a decades-long agreement
treating a nodding homeowner as an understanding one
letting an expiring-discount device back in as a manager-approved exception
acceptance_tests: the homeowner restates the payment obligation, the term and the cancellation right in their own words before signature
no offer in the pack or the conversation is conditioned on signing during the visit
where an interpreter was needed, a competent independent one was used and recorded
revisit_triggers: a signed household later shows they did not understand a core term
a cancellation or complaint cites pressure
a jurisdiction adds language-of-negotiation or vulnerable-consumer requirements

base.update_signal: cancellation and complaint records showing which appointment conditions preceded them, and any new vulnerable-consumer or language-access requirement in the jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Assemble the artifact the household keeps and shows to other people: a one-page plain-language summary of what is being installed, what it is modeled to produce and what the payment obligation is; an assumption page listing the baseline, the rate schedule, the export class, the escalation cases, the loss assumptions and the weather dataset; a site-facts page carrying shade, roof-condition flags and the possibility of a service upgrade with its decision path; the financing disclosure for the chosen class; the incentive statement with its adviser-referral wording; the timeline as staged ranges; and the cancellation-rights notice required by the applicable obligation class. Ordering is part of the design: obligations and uncertainties appear before the savings figure rather than in a back appendix, because a pack that buries them is dishonest even when every individual page is true.

included: the fixed contents of the pack and the order they appear in
the assumption page and the site-facts page as mandatory components
attaching the cancellation-rights notice for the applicable obligation class
excluded: the installation contract and its terms, which are the installer's document
the lender's or third-party owner's own agreements, which are attached rather than authored
marketing collateral about the company, which is not part of the disclosure pack

pros.claim: A fixed pack makes proposal quality independent of which rep built it and gives the household something a neighbour or an adult child can review without the seller present
pros.example: an adult child reading the assumption page a week later can see the baseline, the export class and the escalation cases without calling anyone

cons.claim: A complete pack is long, and length itself reduces the chance any of it is read, which is why ordering and the plain-language summary have to carry the weight
cons.example: a household presented with a thick pack reads the first page and the price, so anything left to the appendix effectively did not get disclosed

failure_modes: shipping the savings page without the assumption page attached to it
leaving the cancellation notice out because the deal was written at an office rather than in the home
letting a rep reorder the pack so the price leads
acceptance_tests: every required component is present and in the specified order
the assumption page is physically adjacent to the savings figure it supports
the cancellation-rights notice matching the applicable obligation class is attached
revisit_triggers: an obligation class or required notice changes
a partner changes the documents that must be attached
households repeatedly ask a question the pack was supposed to answer

base.update_signal: the questions households ask after receiving the pack, which reveal which component failed to communicate, plus any change in required notices

nodes.definition: Run a fixed self-audit before any household is asked to sign, and treat a failed item as a stop rather than as a note. Every number traces to a ledger artifact; no guarantee language appears anywhere; production is labelled as modeled with its band; escalation assumptions are stated and the zero-escalation case is shown; the financing class has been walked and the household can restate the payment obligation, the escalator and the transfer-at-sale rule in their own words; site risks — roof life, probable service upgrade, shade, association restrictions — are written into the proposal rather than left for the installer's site audit to discover; incentives carry the adviser referral; the cancellation-rights notice is attached; and no pressure device was used at any point. This gate is the last place the subdomain can catch a defect for the price of an awkward conversation instead of for the price of a cancellation, a clawback and a neighbourhood story.

included: the fixed pre-signature audit list and the stop-on-fail rule
the household comprehension restatement as a gate item
written site-risk disclosure as a condition of proceeding
excluded: the installer's own post-signature site audit and design verification
credit decisioning, which is the finance provider's gate
post-signature cancellation handling, which belongs to the installer-partnership KB

pros.claim: A stop-on-fail gate is what makes every upstream integrity rule real, because it is the only point where breaking one has an immediate consequence for the seller
pros.example: a proposal whose monthly-savings line cannot be traced to a ledger artifact does not go to signature, no matter how ready the household is

cons.claim: The gate stops deals at the most expensive possible moment for the seller, when the appointment is done and the household is ready to sign
cons.example: a household that has cleared its evening to sign is asked to wait while a missing tariff artifact is retrieved, and momentum is lost

failure_modes: running the gate as a mental checklist rather than a recorded one
waiving an item because the household is impatient
auditing the document while ignoring what was said verbally in the room
acceptance_tests: the audit is recorded per deal with each item marked pass or stop
no deal proceeds to signature with an unresolved stop item
the comprehension restatement is recorded in the household's own words rather than as a tick
revisit_triggers: a cancellation, complaint or dispute traces to an item the gate should have caught
